hypotheses.justification: Its only use is passing it to abs_eigenvector_of_top_eigenvector. That lemma's proof never uses its _hT_compact argument. Inline that proof without compactness; the remaining proof is unchanged. This works for arbitrary measure spaces, including degenerate ones.

A direct argument avoids self-adjointness. Put h = |f|, u = h + f and v = h - f, both nonnegative. If both are nonzero, positivity improvement gives ⟨u,Tv⟩ > 0 and ⟨v,Tu⟩ > 0. Indeed, L2.inner_def and L2.integrable_inner reduce this to nonnegative integrable products; integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae and Lp.eq_zero_iff_ae_eq_zero exclude zero integrals. Bilinearity gives 2(⟨h,Th⟩ − ⟨f,Tf⟩) = ⟨u,Tv⟩ + ⟨v,Tu⟩ > 0, contradicting hlam₀_top, hf_eigen and ‖|f|‖ = ‖f‖. Thus u or v is zero, so f or −f is nonnegative and nonzero. Apply ground_state_strictly_positive to that eigenvector. Empty or zero-measure cases contradict hf_ne.

This follows from the remaining assumptions. Set h = |f|, which is nonnegative and nonzero by hf_ne. Positivity improvement makes Th strictly positive almost everywhere, hence ⟨h,Th⟩ > 0: use L2.inner_def, L2.integrable_inner and integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae; a zero integral would force h = 0 by Lp.eq_zero_iff_ae_eq_zero. Then hlam₀_top gives 0 < ⟨h,Th⟩ ≤ lam₀ * ‖h‖², forcing lam₀ > 0. Recover this fact and use the original proof. Integrability rules out junk integral values; hf_ne excludes zero-measure and trivial Lp cases.
